Who we work with / For property owners

A WEBSITE FOR your property.

Endcap designs websites for owners of a single building or small center who have space to lease. The site belongs to you, so it stays in place through broker changes and between listings, and it carries the availability, plans, your photos and a brochure. A QR code on the sign and a matching flyer send every prospect to the same address.

Let’s talk What’s included

What’s included

What the site includes

Every site is designed and built by Endcap, with the pages, forms, and integrations agreed in your proposal.

01

An address you own

The domain is registered to you and used on the sign, in broker emails and in portal listings, and it stays the same after a listing ends.

02

Availability and plans

Each available suite is shown with size, condition and a plan, and the page is updated when space leases.

03

A QR code on the sign

A code on the leasing sign opens the property page on a phone, so someone passing the property can see the space before calling.

04

A matching flyer

The flyer or brochure is designed with the website, so the PDF a broker attaches and the link they send show the same facts.

05

Calls that reach someone

A phone number people can tap to call and an inquiry form both go to you or your broker, with the property and suite named.

06

Simple updates

You send changes by email or text, and they are made under website care, which includes up to an hour of changes a month with no long-term contract.

  • A number that gets answeredThe phone number on the sign should reach a person, or a voicemail someone checks every day, and the website should list the same number.
  • QR codes that scanPrint the code large enough to scan where people stand or park, link it to a page built for phones, and test it on the printed proof before the sign is made.
  • The domain in your nameRegister the domain to the ownership entity rather than a broker or vendor, so the address stays with the property when relationships change.
  • CASp disclosure in CaliforniaUnder Civil Code §1938, California owners must state on every commercial lease whether the property has undergone a Certified Access Specialist (CASp) inspection. An inspection is not required, but knowing the property’s status before marketing starts prepares you for a tenant’s questions. Source

FAQ

QUESTIONS,
answered.

Anything else? Ask us directly or email Noah at hello@endcap.design.

Why have a website if the space is already on LoopNet?

A portal listing usually sits under the broker’s brand and ends when the listing does. Your own site keeps one address for the sign, the flyer and emails, and it works alongside the portal listing.

Can my broker still be the contact?

Yes. The site can list your broker as the leasing contact and send inquiries to them, to you or to both.

Can you use the photos and plans I already have?

Yes. Send what you have, and we will tell you what is missing or needs work before the site and flyer are designed.

What happens to the site after the space leases?

The site stays live and can show the property and its tenants until the next vacancy. Website care keeps hosting and updates in place with no long-term contract.

How long does a property website take?

Most websites take two to four weeks once the content is ready. A single property site has fewer pages than most, and the proposal confirms its schedule.

What does a property website cost?

Projects are quoted after a short conversation about the property and the materials you have. Scope, timing and price are agreed in writing before work begins.
